claim: Shared-core plus new-vector learning after the 4B-to-8B upgrade met the prespecified new-task acquisition and average old-task retention gates on the screen and fresh confirmation fixture.
limits: One skill family, two fixtures and one training seed per fixture; no estimate of broad task or training-seed variability.
Core training has more trainable parameters than LoRA and adds 96 old-task replay examples.
LoRA reaches 100 percent on both fixtures; this is a mechanism-feasibility result, not a superiority or efficiency result.
Externally supplied task identity; four-choice likelihood scoring; public old-task retention sample.
The untouched 1.7B alignment did not transport the newly learned core skill successfully on either fixture.
The vector-only arm passes its point learning gate only on the fresh fixture and is not a replicated acquisition result.
Full-tensor invariants and four-probe fresh-process equalities rely on recorded execution checks; the independent analysis does not reload GPU tensors.
The fresh fixture has a different hidden mapping, but 12 test input triples overlap the screen test and 13 overlap screen training; every run starts anew from the published initialization.

One old-task BoolQ prompt was truncated. Some equivalent old-task score arrays vary while predicted labels and all new-task baselines remain consistent; this does not establish full-evaluation score equality.
